0.0.n: Introduces the next action in a casual, conversational way.

0.2.n: The plain form comes before 前 to describe the action that happens later.

0.3.n: Follows a plain present-form verb to express doing something earlier than that action.

0.4.n: Marks 寝る前 as the time when the alarm is set.

0.5.n: A borrowed word written in katakana, used here for a wake-up alarm.

0.6.n: Marks アラーム as the thing being set.

0.7.n: Polite form of かける; with アラーム, it describes setting an alarm.

1.0.n: A time word placed first to frame the speaker’s plan.

1.1.n: Marks 明日 as the topic: the speaker is talking about tomorrow.

1.2.n: 時 follows a number to give an hour of the day.

1.3.n: Marks 8時 as the specific time the speaker wants to wake up.

1.4.n: 起きる becomes 起きたい by replacing る with たい to express the speaker’s wish.

1.5.n: Introduces the reason for the alarm times that follow.

2.0.n: 半 after an hour means half past that hour.

2.1.n: Connects the first alarm time to the next one in the list.

2.3.n: Gives the hour; the following 45分 supplies the minutes.

2.4.n: 分 marks minutes; after 7時, this makes the time 7:45.

2.5.n: Links 7:45 to another alarm time in the list.

2.7.n: Gives the hour; the following 50分 supplies the minutes.

2.8.n: 分 marks minutes; after 7時, this makes the time 7:50.

3.0.n: Adds the final alarm time to the preceding list.

3.1.n: Names the final alarm time, matching the speaker’s desired wake-up time.

3.2.n: Marks 8時 as the time the alarm should ring, not when the speaker sets it.

3.3.n: Japanese nouns do not require plural endings, so this can cover all the alarms listed.

3.4.n: Marks アラーム as what the speaker will set.

3.5.n: The polite ます form describes the planned action here, rather than an action happening now.

0.lit: Well then, before going to bed, I will set an alarm.
0.tip: Use a plain present-form verb plus 前に to say before doing something.

1.lit: As for tomorrow, because I want to wake up at eight o’clock…
1.tip: ので gives a reason and connects this unfinished line to the action that follows.

2.lit: Seven thirty and seven forty-five and seven fifty…
2.tip: 半 means half past; 時 and 分 mark hours and minutes.

3.lit: And then, for eight o’clock, I will set an alarm.
3.tip: With アラームをかけます, the time marked by に is when the alarm should ring.
